cases.note: The write's output_hash is SHA-256(JCS({content_sha256, decision_id})), claimed decision_id recomputes from the given decision_preimage, and that decision's outcome is permit. This is the positive case: ordering is established by hash dependency alone.

output_hash is the legacy content-only commitment (today's shape in ../build_vectors.py). Not tampering -- the write simply predates or does not use this mechanism. Reported as unverifiable, never as a failure.

claimed_decision_id is an arbitrary value that does not recompute from decision_preimage's own fields -- the citation of WHICH decision covers this write is itself wrong or fabricated, caught before even checking the output binding.

claimed_decision_id correctly recomputes from decision_preimage (the citation is legitimate), but recorded_output_hash was actually computed against a different decision_id (other_decision_id) -- neither the bound form under the claimed id nor the legacy form matches. Someone swapped which decision the output is really bound to after citing this one.

output_hash correctly binds to denied_decision_id, which recomputes cleanly from its own preimage -- but that decision's outcome is 'deny'. A denied decision cannot be the covering authority for a write that happened anyway, even though the binding itself is cryptographically sound. Same lesson as PROVENANCE.md finding #6 applied here.

Same content_sha256 and decision_id as DECISION-BOUND-OK. prior_unbound_commitment shows a legacy (content-only) commitment for this exact content was already on record before the bound commitment existed -- evidence the effect may have happened before any binding, not after. verify_case() ignores prior_unbound_commitment and still returns COMMITMENT_AFTER_DECISION: this vector demonstrates the documented commitment-after-decision vs write-after-decision gap (decision_bound.py module docstring), it does not close it. Comparable to EIP-3009 only in the positive direction -- EIP-3009's nonce is consumed by the same event that moves funds, so there is no equivalent unbound path for a payment; a file write has no single choke point like that unless a sink is defined to accept only bound writes, which is outside this mechanism.

ogasurfproject-jpg's reader-C/B clean-room comparison (2026-10-14, second blind round against 4cbf5c8): same forged claimed_decision_id as DECISION-BOUND-FORGED-CITATION, but recorded_output_hash is the UNBOUND legacy form, not a bound-mismatch value. Pins that the citation check happens strictly before the output hash is even built -- a forged citation is caught regardless of what the recorded output hash looks like, legacy or not.

ogasurfproject-jpg's reader-C/B clean-room comparison (2026-10-14, second blind round against 4cbf5c8): same denied decision as DECISION-BOUND-DENIED (outcome=deny, citation recomputes cleanly), but recorded_output_hash is the UNBOUND legacy form. Pins that the legacy-hash check runs before the outcome=permit gate -- an unbound write is ORDERING_UNVERIFIABLE even when the decision it might have cited was denied, never UNAUTHORIZED_BINDING, because no binding to that decision was ever claimed by the hash itself.

ogasurfproject-jpg's reader-C/B clean-room comparison (2026-10-14, second blind round against 4cbf5c8): same denied decision as DECISION-BOUND-DENIED, but recorded_output_hash matches neither the bound form under the cited (denied) decision_id nor the legacy content-only form -- reuses DECISION-BOUND-SUBSTITUTED's own mismatch value. Pins that an unrelated/altered output hash is BINDING_MISMATCH even when the cited decision was denied, never UNAUTHORIZED_BINDING, because UNAUTHORIZED_BINDING requires the recorded hash to actually match the bound form first.
